    number_of_grades INTEGER DEFAULT 3,
    multi_product_dispenser BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    blended_products_supported BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,

    -- Connected tanks
    connected_tanks JSONB, -- Array of tank IDs and grade mappings

    -- Display and interface
    display_type VARCHAR(30) DEFAULT 'lcd', -- lcd, led, mechanical
    price_sign_integrated BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    payment_terminal_integrated BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,

    -- Dispensing capabilities
    maximum_flow_rate_lpm DECIMAL(6,2), -- Liters per minute
    minimum_dispensing_amount DECIMAL(6,2) DEFAULT 0.01,
    maximum_dispensing_amount DECIMAL(8,2) DEFAULT 999.99,

    -- Safety features
    emergency_stop_button BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,

    -- Maintenance

    next_calibration_due_date DATE,
    last_maintenance_date DATE,
    maintenance_interval_days INTEGER DEFAULT 30,

    -- Status
    dispenser_status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active', -- active, maintenance, out_of_order, decommissioned

    -- Regulatory compliance
    weights_measures_seal_number VARCHAR(50),
    seal_date DATE,
    permit_numbers JSONB,

    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),

    CONSTRAINT valid_dispenser_status CHECK (dispenser_status IN ('active', 'maintenance', 'out_of_order', 'decommissioned')),
    UNIQUE(site_id, dispenser_number)
);

-- Fuel transactions (individual fuel sales)
CREATE TABLE fuel_transactions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

    -- Transaction identification
    transaction_number VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    pos_transaction_id VARCHAR(100), -- Link to POS system

    -- Dispenser and location
    dispenser_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES fuel_dispensers(id),
    hose_number INTEGER NOT NULL,

    -- Customer and payment
    customer_id UUID REFERENCES customers(id),
    fleet_card_number VARCHAR(50),
    payment_method VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, -- cash, credit_card, debit_card, fleet_card, prepaid

    -- Fuel details
    fuel_product_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES fuel_products(id),
    fuel_grade VARCHAR(50),

    -- Transaction amounts
    gallons_dispensed DECIMAL(10,4) NOT NULL,
    price_per_gallon DECIMAL(6,4) NOT NULL,
    fuel_amount DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
    taxes_amount DECIMAL(8,2) DEFAULT 0,
    total_amount DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,

    -- Transaction timing
    transaction_start_time TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    transaction_end_time TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,

    -- Vehicle information (for fleet cards)
    vehicle_id VARCHAR(50),
    odometer_reading INTEGER,
    driver_id VARCHAR(50),
    vehicle_license_plate VARCHAR(20),

    -- Loyalty and discounts
    loyalty_card_number VARCHAR(50),
    discount_amount DECIMAL(6,2) DEFAULT 0,
    loyalty_points_earned INTEGER DEFAULT 0,

    -- Transaction status
    transaction_status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'completed', -- completed, cancelled, voided, disputed

    -- Regulatory reporting
    reported_to_state BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    state_reporting_date DATE,

    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),

    CONSTRAINT valid_payment_method CHECK (payment_method IN ('cash', 'credit_card', 'debit_card', 'fleet_card', 'prepaid')),
    CONSTRAINT valid_transaction_status CHECK (transaction_status IN ('completed', 'cancelled', 'voided', 'disputed'))
);

-- Dispenser price management
CREATE TABLE dispenser_prices (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

    -- Price identification
    dispenser_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES fuel_dispensers(id),
    fuel_product_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES fuel_products(id),

    -- Pricing details
    current_price DECIMAL(6,4) NOT NULL,
    previous_price DECIMAL(6,4),
    cost_basis DECIMAL(6,4), -- Wholesale cost basis
    margin_amount DECIMAL(6,4),
    margin_percentage DECIMAL(5,2),

    -- Price timing
    price_effective_date TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    price_change_reason VARCHAR(100),

    -- Competitive pricing
    competitor_average_price DECIMAL(6,4),
    market_position VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'competitive', -- low, competitive, high

    -- Promotional pricing
    promotional_price DECIMAL(6,4),
    promotion_start_date TIMESTAMPTZ,
    promotion_end_date TIMESTAMPTZ,
    promotion_description TEXT,

    -- Price management
    auto_pricing_enabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    price_update_frequency_hours INTEGER DEFAULT 24,
    maximum_price_change_percentage DECIMAL(5,2) DEFAULT 10,

    -- Approval requirements
    requires_manager_approval BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    approved_by UUID REFERENCES employees(id),
    approved_at TIMESTAMPTZ,

    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),

    CONSTRAINT valid_market_position CHECK (market_position IN ('low', 'competitive', 'high')),
    UNIQUE(dispenser_id, fuel_product_id)
);

docs.title: Fleet Customer Management
docs.text:
interface FleetManagementSystem {
  processFleetTransaction(transactionData: FleetTransactionData): Promise<FleetTransactionResult>;
  validateFleetCard(cardNumber: string, pin?: string): Promise<CardValidationResult>;
  manageFuelLimits(fleetAccountId: string, limits: FuelLimits): Promise<void>;
  generateFleetReports(fleetAccountId: string, period: DateRange): Promise<FleetReport>;
}

interface FleetTransactionData {
  card_number: string;
  pin?: string;
  vehicle_id?: string;
  driver_id?: string;
  odometer_reading?: number;
  fuel_type: string;
  gallons: number;
  price_per_gallon: number;
  location_id: string;
  transaction_timestamp: Date;
}

interface FleetTransactionResult {
  approved: boolean;
  transaction_id?: string;
  authorization_code?: string;
  decline_reason?: string;
  remaining_limits: {
    daily_gallons: number;
    daily_amount: number;
    monthly_gallons: number;
    monthly_amount: number;
  };
}

interface FuelLimits {
  daily_gallon_limit: number;
  daily_dollar_limit: number;
  monthly_gallon_limit: number;
  monthly_dollar_limit: number;
  allowed_fuel_types: string[];
  allowed_locations: string[];
  time_restrictions: TimeRestriction[];
  product_restrictions: ProductRestriction[];
}

// Fleet accounts and customers
const fleetAccountsSchema = `
CREATE TABLE fleet_accounts (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

    -- Account identification
    account_number VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    company_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,

    -- Billing and contact
    billing_address JSONB NOT NULL,
    primary_contact_name VARCHAR(255),
    primary_contact_email VARCHAR(255),
    primary_contact_phone VARCHAR(20),

    -- Account settings
    account_type VARCHAR(30) DEFAULT 'commercial', -- commercial, government, non_profit
    credit_limit DECIMAL(15,2) DEFAULT 0,
    payment_terms_days INTEGER DEFAULT 30,

    -- Fuel program settings
    fuel_discount_percentage DECIMAL(5,2) DEFAULT 0,
    volume_discount_tiers JSONB, -- Volume-based discount structure

    -- Controls and restrictions
    pin_required BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    odometer_required BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    driver_id_required BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,

    -- Default limits (can be overridden per card)
    default_daily_gallon_limit DECIMAL(8,2) DEFAULT 999.99,
    default_daily_dollar_limit DECIMAL(10,2) DEFAULT 9999.99,
    default_monthly_gallon_limit DECIMAL(10,2) DEFAULT 99999.99,
    default_monthly_dollar_limit DECIMAL(12,2) DEFAULT 999999.99,

    -- Allowed products and locations
    allowed_fuel_products JSONB, -- Array of fuel product IDs
    allowed_locations JSONB, -- Array of site IDs or 'all'
    restricted_locations JSONB, -- Array of restricted site IDs

    -- Account status
    account_status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active', -- active, suspended, closed
    credit_status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'approved', -- approved, hold, suspended

    -- Billing and reporting
    billing_cycle VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'monthly', -- weekly, monthly, custom
    statement_delivery_method VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'email', -- email, postal, electronic

    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),

    CONSTRAINT valid_account_type CHECK (account_type IN ('commercial', 'government', 'non_profit')),
    CONSTRAINT valid_account_status CHECK (account_status IN ('active', 'suspended', 'closed')),
    CONSTRAINT valid_credit_status CHECK (credit_status IN ('approved', 'hold', 'suspended')),
    CONSTRAINT valid_billing_cycle CHECK (billing_cycle IN ('weekly', 'monthly', 'custom'))
);

-- Fleet cards issued to account
CREATE TABLE fleet_cards (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    fleet_account_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES fleet_accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

    -- Card identification
    card_number VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    card_type VARCHAR(30) DEFAULT 'fuel_only', -- fuel_only, fuel_and_maintenance, universal

    -- Vehicle and driver assignment
    vehicle_id VARCHAR(50),
    vehicle_description VARCHAR(255),
    license_plate VARCHAR(20),
    vin VARCHAR(17),
    assigned_driver_id VARCHAR(50),
    assigned_driver_name VARCHAR(255),

    -- Card security
    pin_hash VARCHAR(255), -- Hashed PIN
    security_code VARCHAR(10),

    -- Card limits (overrides account defaults if set)
    daily_gallon_limit DECIMAL(8,2),
    daily_dollar_limit DECIMAL(10,2),
    monthly_gallon_limit DECIMAL(10,2),
    monthly_dollar_limit DECIMAL(12,2),

    -- Usage restrictions
    allowed_fuel_products JSONB, -- Override account settings if specified
    allowed_day_of_week JSONB, -- Array of allowed days (1-7)
    allowed_time_start TIME,
    allowed_time_end TIME,

    -- Current usage tracking
    current_month_gallons DECIMAL(10,2) DEFAULT 0,
    current_month_amount DECIMAL(12,2) DEFAULT 0,
    current_day_gallons DECIMAL(8,2) DEFAULT 0,
    current_day_amount DECIMAL(10,2) DEFAULT 0,
    last_reset_date DATE DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE,

    -- Card status
    card_status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active', -- active, suspended, lost, stolen, expired
    issue_date DATE NOT NULL,
    expiry_date DATE,
    last_used_date DATE,

    -- Security flags
    compromised BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    fraud_suspected BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    velocity_check_enabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,

    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),

    CONSTRAINT valid_card_type CHECK (card_type IN ('fuel_only', 'fuel_and_maintenance', 'universal')),
    CONSTRAINT valid_card_status CHECK (card_status IN ('active', 'suspended', 'lost', 'stolen', 'expired'))
);`;

class FleetCardService implements FleetManagementSystem {
  async processFleetTransaction(transactionData: FleetTransactionData): Promise<FleetTransactionResult> {
    // Step 1: Validate card
    const cardValidation = await this.validateFleetCard(transactionData.card_number, transactionData.pin);
    if (!cardValidation.valid) {
      return {
        approved: false,
        decline_reason: cardValidation.decline_reason
      };
    }

    const fleetCard = cardValidation.card;
    const fleetAccount = await this.getFleetAccount(fleetCard.fleet_account_id);

    // Step 2: Check limits
    const limitsCheck = await this.checkTransactionLimits(fleetCard, transactionData);
    if (!limitsCheck.approved) {
      return {
        approved: false,
        decline_reason: limitsCheck.reason
      };
    }

    // Step 3: Check restrictions
    const restrictionsCheck = this.checkTransactionRestrictions(fleetCard, fleetAccount, transactionData);
    if (!restrictionsCheck.approved) {
      return {
        approved: false,
        decline_reason: restrictionsCheck.reason
      };
    }

    // Step 4: Process transaction
    const transaction = await this.createFleetTransaction({
      fleet_card_id: fleetCard.id,
      fleet_account_id: fleetAccount.id,
      ...transactionData,
      authorized: true,
      authorization_code: this.generateAuthorizationCode()
    });

    // Step 5: Update usage tracking
    await this.updateCardUsage(fleetCard.id, transactionData.gallons, 
      transactionData.gallons * transactionData.price_per_gallon);

    // Step 6: Apply discounts
    const discountedAmount = this.calculateFleetDiscount(
      transactionData.gallons * transactionData.price_per_gallon,
      fleetAccount.fuel_discount_percentage,
      fleetAccount.volume_discount_tiers,
      await this.getMonthlyVolume(fleetAccount.id)
    );

    return {
      approved: true,
      transaction_id: transaction.id,
      authorization_code: transaction.authorization_code,
      remaining_limits: await this.getRemainingLimits(fleetCard.id)
    };
  }

  async validateFleetCard(cardNumber: string, pin?: string): Promise<CardValidationResult> {
    const card = await this.getFleetCardByNumber(cardNumber);

    if (!card) {
      return { valid: false, decline_reason: 'Invalid card number' };
    }

    if (card.card_status !== 'active') {
      return { valid: false, decline_reason: `Card is ${card.card_status}` };
    }

    if (card.expiry_date && new Date(card.expiry_date) < new Date()) {
      return { valid: false, decline_reason: 'Card expired' };
    }

    // Validate PIN if required
    const account = await this.getFleetAccount(card.fleet_account_id);
    if (account.pin_required && pin) {
      const pinValid = await this.validatePin(card.pin_hash, pin);
      if (!pinValid) {
        return { valid: false, decline_reason: 'Invalid PIN' };
      }
    }

    // Check account status
    if (account.account_status !== 'active') {
      return { valid: false, decline_reason: `Account is ${account.account_status}` };
    }

    if (account.credit_status !== 'approved') {
      return { valid: false, decline_reason: 'Account credit hold' };
    }

    return { valid: true, card, account };
  }

  private async checkTransactionLimits(card: FleetCard, transaction: FleetTransactionData): Promise<{approved: boolean, reason?: string}> {
    const transactionAmount = transaction.gallons * transaction.price_per_gallon;

    // Check daily gallon limit
    const dailyGallonLimit = card.daily_gallon_limit || card.fleet_account.default_daily_gallon_limit;
    if (card.current_day_gallons + transaction.gallons > dailyGallonLimit) {
      return { approved: false, reason: 'Daily gallon limit exceeded' };
    }

    // Check daily dollar limit
    const dailyDollarLimit = card.daily_dollar_limit || card.fleet_account.default_daily_dollar_limit;
    if (card.current_day_amount + transactionAmount > dailyDollarLimit) {
      return { approved: false, reason: 'Daily dollar limit exceeded' };
    }

    // Check monthly limits
    const monthlyGallonLimit = card.monthly_gallon_limit || card.fleet_account.default_monthly_gallon_limit;
    if (card.current_month_gallons + transaction.gallons > monthlyGallonLimit) {
      return { approved: false, reason: 'Monthly gallon limit exceeded' };
    }

    const monthlyDollarLimit = card.monthly_dollar_limit || card.fleet_account.default_monthly_dollar_limit;
    if (card.current_month_amount + transactionAmount > monthlyDollarLimit) {
      return { approved: false, reason: 'Monthly dollar limit exceeded' };
    }

    return { approved: true };
  }

  private calculateFleetDiscount(
    baseAmount: number, 
    discountPercentage: number, 
    volumeTiers: any[], 
    monthlyVolume: number
  ): number {

    let discount = baseAmount * (discountPercentage / 100);

    // Apply volume-based discounts
    if (volumeTiers && volumeTiers.length > 0) {
      for (const tier of volumeTiers.sort((a, b) => b.minimum_gallons - a.minimum_gallons)) {
        if (monthlyVolume >= tier.minimum_gallons) {
          const volumeDiscount = baseAmount * (tier.discount_percentage / 100);
          discount = Math.max(discount, volumeDiscount);
          break;
        }
      }
    }

    return baseAmount - discount;
  }
}

This forecourt management system provides sophisticated fuel inventory control, pump operations, environmental compliance, and fleet card processing capabilities specifically designed for gas stations and fuel retail operations while integrating seamlessly with the core ERP financial, inventory, and customer management modules.

docs.title: 1.1 Build on What Exists
docs.text:
The Forecourt module is not a standalone silo. A petrol station is at its core a retail business that receives goods (fuel deliveries), stores them (tanks), sells them (pump transactions), employs staff (attendants and cashiers), and reports financial results (GL). Every one of those activities has a home in an existing Awo ERP module.

The Forecourt module's job is to:

  1. Extend existing modules with domain-specific concepts (a tank is a warehouse with extra physical attributes; a fuel grade is a product with density and temperature sensitivity; a cashier session is an HR shift with a till float).
  2. Orchestrate the operational workflow unique to forecourt: meter readings, dip readings, shift reconciliation, and wetstock variance.
  3. Produce the downstream artifacts that the Finance, Inventory, and HR modules consume — without duplicating their data.

docs.title: 1.2 What the Forecourt Module Does NOT Own
docs.text: Concern Owned By Fuel product catalogue (grade, unit) Inventory — product with category = FUEL Tank as a storage location Inventory — warehouse/location with type = TANK Fuel delivery receiving Procurement — purchase receipt against a PO Pump transaction as a sale Sales — sales order / POS transaction Cashier and attendant as employees HR — employee record Shift scheduling and attendance HR — shift record, clock-in/out General ledger journals Finance GL — journal batch Accounts receivable (credit customers) Finance AR — invoice and receivable Supplier management Procurement — supplier record

docs.title: 1.3 What the Forecourt Module Does Own
docs.text:
• Physical infrastructure: Pumps, nozzles, and their relationships to tanks and products.
  • Meter readings: Cumulative totalizer values on nozzles — a concept that has no equivalent elsewhere in the ERP.
  • Dip readings: Tank level measurements — physical observations unique to wetstock management.
  • Forecourt shift context: The operational wrapper around an HR shift that adds a till float, meter snapshots, cash pickups, and a reconciliation.
  • Cash management events: Floats, pickups, and safe drops that happen during a shift.
  • Wetstock reconciliation: The computed comparison of theoretical vs actual fuel volume in a tank.
  • Fleet card operations: Per-card fuel limits, usage tracking, and commercial account management.
  • Environmental compliance records: Leak detection tests, spill incidents, and regulatory compliance tracking.

docs.title: 2. Domain Overview — The Forecourt Business
docs.text: Before we model data, we must understand the business. A petroleum retail site is fundamentally a volume business. Revenue is generated by dispensing measured litres of fuel. Every business control — cash management, stock control, theft prevention, regulatory compliance — ultimately traces back to controlling and accounting for volume.

docs.title: 2.1 The Physical Site
docs.text:
A forecourt is organised as follows:

Site (Shell Maanzoni Service Station)
│
├── Tanks (underground storage)
│     Each tank holds exactly one fuel grade.
│     Tanks are the inventory source of truth for volume.
│
├── Pumps (dispensing islands on the forecourt)
│     Each pump island has one or more pump units.
│     A pump unit has one or more nozzles (hoses).
│     Each nozzle is connected to exactly one tank.
│
└── POS / Cashier Station
      Cash is collected here.
      Sales are recorded here.
      The cashier reconciles here at shift end.

docs.title: 2.2 The Money Flow
docs.text:
Customer pays
      ↓
Cash / MPesa / Card / Fleet Card collected at POS
      ↓
Expected cash = Volume dispensed × Unit price
      ↓
Cashier declared cash vs expected cash → Cash variance (over/short)
      ↓
Revenue posted to GL

docs.title: 2.3 The Fuel Flow
docs.text:
Delivery arrives (truck from depot)
      ↓
Dip reading BEFORE delivery
      ↓
Fuel pumped into tank (volume from truck docket + dip after)
      ↓
Stock increases in tank
      ↓
Throughout shift: customers draw fuel through nozzles
      ↓
Each nozzle's cumulative meter increases
      ↓
Volume sold = closing meter − opening meter
      ↓
Dip reading at shift end
      ↓
Theoretical stock = opening dip + deliveries − volume sold
Actual stock = closing dip
Wetstock variance = theoretical − actual

docs.title: 2.4 The Daily Operating Cycle
docs.text: A petrol station typically runs 24 hours across two or three overlapping shifts. Each shift is the primary unit of accountability. The day is controlled not by the clock but by the shift handover. At every handover, physical readings (meters, dips, cash) are captured, handed from outgoing cashier to incoming cashier, and reconciled. This is the heartbeat of the forecourt business.

docs.title: 2.5 Why Variance Matters
docs.text:
A wetstock loss of even 0.5% on a site moving 50,000 litres per day is 250 litres — roughly KES 37,500 — every single day. Over a year that is KES 13.7 million in losses that may be from:

  • Evaporation and temperature effects — normal and expected within tolerance.
  • Meter drift — pump meters that under-read (dispense more than they record).
  • Delivery short-delivery — supplier delivering less than the docket states.
  • Theft — by staff (meter manipulation, short-fill) or by customers (drive-offs).
  • Tank leaks — a regulatory and environmental emergency.

The wetstock reconciliation system is therefore not administrative overhead — it is the primary fraud and loss-prevention control for the business.

docs.title: Inventory Module — Products & Warehouses
docs.text:
The Inventory module is extended with two domain-specific types. No new product or warehouse table is created; instead the existing records gain forecourt attributes via extension tables.

Fuel product is an Inventory product where: - category = 'FUEL' - It has a corresponding forecourt_product_attributes row with fuel-specific fields (density, temperature correction factor, colour code).

Tank is an Inventory warehouse/location where: - location_type = 'TANK' - It has a corresponding forecourt_tank_attributes row with physical tank data (capacity, safe fill, ATG device reference).

All stock movements — deliveries in, sales out — are posted as standard Inventory stock transactions. The forecourt module triggers these; it does not own them.

docs.title: Procurement Module — Deliveries
docs.text:
A fuel delivery is a Purchase Receipt in Procurement terms. The Procurement module owns the purchase order, goods receipt, and supplier invoice. The Forecourt module enriches the receipt with: - Dip readings before and after delivery. - Temperature-corrected volume. - Delivery docket number and truck registration.

The Forecourt module listens for procurement.goods_receipt.confirmed events to update wetstock calculations. It does not duplicate the receipt data.

docs.title: HR Module — Shifts & Staff
docs.text:
A forecourt shift is an HR Shift with a forecourt context wrapper. The HR shift owns shift start/end times, employee clock-in/out, and break periods.

The Forecourt module creates a forecourt_shift_context record linked to the HR shift, adding till float amount, opening/closing meter snapshots, cash pickup events, and the reconciliation result.

When the HR module closes a shift (employee clocks out), the Forecourt module is notified and initiates the close pipeline.

docs.title: Sales Module — POS Transactions
docs.text: Each fuel dispense is a Sales transaction. The Sales module owns the sale record, payment method, and customer (for credit sales). The Forecourt module adds the nozzle that dispensed the fuel, the volume dispensed (from meter delta or pump controller), and the shift context the sale belongs to.

docs.title: Finance GL — Journals
docs.text: The Forecourt module does not create GL journal lines directly. It calls the Finance GL service with a structured journal request at shift close. The Finance module owns the journal, the accounts, and the posting logic. The Forecourt module provides the business context.

docs.title: 4. Domain Glossary
docs.text: Term Definition ATG Automatic Tank Gauge. An electronic probe system that continuously measures fuel level and temperature inside a tank, typically polling every 15 minutes. Cashier Session The period during which a specific employee is responsible for a specific till. A shift may have multiple cashier sessions if the till is handed over mid-shift. Closing Dip A dip reading taken at the end of a shift or reconciliation period to determine actual closing stock. Dip Reading A measurement of fuel volume (or level in mm) inside a tank at a point in time. Can be manual (using a dip stick or calibration chart) or automated (ATG). Fleet Card A payment card issued to a commercial fleet account. Carries configurable fuel limits per vehicle or driver. Float The seed cash placed in a till at the start of a cashier session to enable making change. Meter Reading The value shown on a nozzle's cumulative totalizer at a specific point in time. Meters never reset; they are monotonically increasing. Nozzle / Hose A single dispensing outlet on a pump. Each nozzle is associated with exactly one tank and fuel grade. A pump may have two or more nozzles for different grades. Opening Dip A dip reading taken at the start of a shift or reconciliation period to establish opening stock. Pickup (Cash) The removal of excess cash from a till to a safe during a shift, to reduce theft risk. Performed by a supervisor and logged. Pump A physical dispensing unit on the forecourt. One pump may serve two sides of an island (hence multiple nozzles). Safe Drop The deposit of bagged cash into the site safe at the end of a shift. Requires dual control (cashier + supervisor). Shift The primary unit of operational and financial accountability for a forecourt. Corresponds to an HR shift but carries additional forecourt context (meters, dips, cash, reconciliation). Tank A physical underground or above-ground vessel that stores a single fuel grade. Represented in the ERP as an Inventory warehouse location of type TANK. Temperature Correction The adjustment of observed fuel volume to a standard temperature of 15°C, accounting for thermal expansion/contraction. Required for accurate wetstock reconciliation. Totalizer The cumulative litre counter on a nozzle. Records every litre ever dispensed through that nozzle since installation. Ullage The empty (unfilled) space in a tank above the fuel surface. Ullage = Capacity − Current Volume. Used to determine safe delivery volume. VCF Volume Correction Factor. Converts observed fuel volume at a measured temperature to the standard 15°C volume. Published by ASTM and OIML. Volume Sold Closing totalizer − Opening totalizer for a nozzle within a defined period. WAC Weighted Average Cost. The inventory valuation method applied to fuel stock. Recalculated with every delivery. Wetstock All liquid fuel held in tanks on the site — the "wet" stock as opposed to lubricants, shop goods, etc. Wetstock Variance Theoretical closing stock − Actual closing stock (dip). Negative = loss; positive = gain.

docs.title: 6. Data Model — Forecourt-Owned Tables Only
docs.text:
The following tables are owned and managed exclusively by the Forecourt module. All other data referenced lives in its home module.

Migration note: The DDL sections below are ordered to satisfy foreign key constraints. forecourt_shift_contexts must be created before forecourt_meter_readings and forecourt_dip_readings, which both reference it.

docs.title: 6.1 Tank Attributes Extension
docs.text:
-- Extends Inventory locations that represent fuel tanks.
-- The canonical record (name, site, is_active) lives in inventory_locations.
CREATE TABLE forecourt_tank_attributes (
    location_id             UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES inventory_locations(id),
    tenant_id               UUID NOT NULL,
    capacity_l              NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    safe_fill_l             NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL, -- max fill without overspill risk
    minimum_operating_l     NUMERIC(10, 2),          -- low-stock alert threshold
    reorder_l               NUMERIC(10, 2),           -- reorder trigger level
    has_atg                 BOOLEAN       NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    atg_device_ref          VARCHAR(100),             -- external ATG system identifier
    atg_manufacturer        VARCHAR(100),
    atg_model               VARCHAR(100),
    -- Tank physical properties
    tank_type               VARCHAR(30) DEFAULT 'underground', -- underground | aboveground | mobile
    tank_material           VARCHAR(30) DEFAULT 'steel',       -- steel | fiberglass | composite
    installation_date       DATE,
    manufacturer            VARCHAR(100),
    -- Calibration and correction
    calibration_chart       JSONB,        -- mm-to-litre lookup table if no ATG
    temp_correction_table   JSONB,        -- [{temp_c, factor}] pairs (ASTM/OIML VCF)
    last_calibration_date   DATE,
    next_calibration_due    DATE,
    -- Environmental compliance
    leak_detection_system   VARCHAR(50),  -- continuous | periodic | manual
    leak_detection_last_test DATE,
    vapor_recovery_system   BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    spill_containment_l     NUMERIC(10, 2),
    -- Regulatory
    permit_number           VARCHAR(100),
    permit_expiry_date      DATE,
    created_at              TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at              TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT valid_tank_type CHECK (tank_type IN ('underground', 'aboveground', 'mobile'))
);

Why JSONB for the calibration chart? Tank calibration tables are provided by manufacturers as mm-to-litre mappings — typically 500–1000 data points. Storing this as JSONB avoids a separate table while keeping it queryable when the application needs to convert a dip-stick reading in mm to litres.

docs.title: 6.2 Product Attributes Extension
docs.text:
-- Extends Inventory products that represent fuel grades.
CREATE TABLE forecourt_product_attributes (
    product_id              UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES inventory_products(id),
    tenant_id               UUID NOT NULL,
    fuel_code               VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,  -- PMS, AGO, DPK, ULSD, LPG
    -- Colour coding follows Kenya/industry convention: RED=PMS, BLACK=AGO, BLUE=DPK
    nozzle_colour_code      VARCHAR(30),
    -- Physical properties for wetstock and temperature correction
    density_kg_l_at_15c     NUMERIC(7, 5),         -- e.g. 0.73500 for PMS
    -- Wetstock loss tolerance thresholds (site can override in config)
    max_loss_pct            NUMERIC(5, 3) DEFAULT 0.500,
    max_gain_pct            NUMERIC(5, 3) DEFAULT 0.300,
    created_at              TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at              TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

docs.title: 6.3 Pumps and Nozzles
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE forecourt_pumps (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id       UUID NOT NULL,
    site_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES sites(id),
    pump_number     INT  NOT NULL,  -- display number on the island (1, 2, 3...)
    name            VARCHAR(100),
    make            VARCHAR(100),   -- Tokheim, Wayne, Gilbarco, etc.
    model           VARCHAR(100),
    serial_number   VARCHAR(100),
    controller_ref  VARCHAR(100),   -- pump controller network address / ID
    -- Dispenser capabilities
    number_of_nozzles       INT,
    max_flow_rate_lpm       NUMERIC(6, 2),
    vapor_recovery_system   BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    payment_terminal        BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    -- Maintenance
    installation_date       DATE,
    last_calibration_date   DATE,
    next_calibration_due    DATE,
    -- Regulatory
    weights_measures_seal   VARCHAR(50),
    seal_date               DATE,
    is_active       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, site_id, pump_number)
);

CREATE TABLE forecourt_nozzles (
    id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id           UUID NOT NULL,
    pump_id             UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES forecourt_pumps(id),
    -- Tank is an Inventory location of type TANK
    tank_location_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES inventory_locations(id),
    -- Fuel product from Inventory
    product_id          UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES inventory_products(id),
    nozzle_number       INT  NOT NULL,  -- 1-based within the pump
    controller_ref      VARCHAR(100),   -- nozzle ID in pump controller system
    is_active           BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, pump_id, nozzle_number)
);

docs.title: 6.4 Shift Context
docs.text:
DDL order: forecourt_shift_contexts is defined here before forecourt_meter_readings and forecourt_dip_readings because both tables carry a foreign key to this table.

CREATE TYPE forecourt_shift_status AS ENUM (
    'OPEN',      -- shift is in progress
    'CLOSING',   -- close pipeline running
    'CLOSED',    -- successfully closed and reconciled
    'DISPUTED',  -- variance exceeds tolerance, awaiting manager approval
    'AMENDED'    -- closed but subsequently amended
);

CREATE TABLE forecourt_shift_contexts (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id       UUID NOT NULL,
    site_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES sites(id),
    -- The HR shift this context wraps. One forecourt context per HR shift.
    hr_shift_id     UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES hr_shifts(id),
    shift_number    BIGINT NOT NULL,  -- sequential per site, for human reference
    status          forecourt_shift_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'OPEN',
    -- Pipeline state tracks completed stages for idempotent re-runs.
    -- Schema: {"completed_at": {"READINGS_VALIDATE": "2024-11-15T07:05:00Z", ...}}
    pipeline_state  JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    opened_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    closed_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
    notes           TEXT,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, site_id, shift_number)
);

docs.title: 6.5 Meter Readings
docs.text:
Meter readings are append-only. The totalizer on a physical nozzle is never reset; it only ever increases. The system must handle the rare case where a meter physically rolls over (returns to zero after reaching its display maximum).

CREATE TABLE forecourt_meter_readings (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id       UUID NOT NULL,
    nozzle_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES forecourt_nozzles(id),
    -- Shift context. NULL only for out-of-shift spot readings (e.g. maintenance check).
    shift_context_id UUID REFERENCES forecourt_shift_contexts(id),
    reading_type    VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    -- SHIFT_OPEN      — captured at shift start
    -- SHIFT_CLOSE     — captured at shift end
    -- SPOT            — ad-hoc reading during shift
    -- AMENDMENT       — correction of a previous reading (references superseded_id)
    -- CONTROLLER_SYNC — imported from pump controller system
    observed_at     TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL,
    totalizer_l     NUMERIC(14, 3) NOT NULL,  -- raw meter display value
    rollover_count  INT           NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    -- effective_l = totalizer_l + (rollover_count × site_rollover_max)
    -- Computed in application code, not stored, to keep readings immutable.
    source          VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'MANUAL',  -- MANUAL | CONTROLLER | IMPORT
    recorded_by     UUID         REFERENCES users(id),
    superseded_by   UUID         REFERENCES forecourt_meter_readings(id),
    notes           TEXT,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    -- NEVER UPDATE. Corrections are new rows with reading_type = 'AMENDMENT'.
);

Rollover handling: When a 6-digit meter (max 999,999.999 L) rolls over, the technician records a new reading with rollover_count = previous_rollover_count + 1. The effective cumulative total is totalizer_l + (rollover_count × 999999.999). Volume sold between two readings is always computed from their effective totals, never from raw totalizer values.

docs.title: 6.6 Dip Readings
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE forecourt_dip_readings (
    id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id           UUID NOT NULL,
    -- The tank (Inventory location)
    tank_location_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES inventory_locations(id),
    -- Shift context if this dip is part of a shift open/close
    shift_context_id    UUID REFERENCES forecourt_shift_contexts(id),
    reading_type        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    -- SHIFT_OPEN         — opening dip for shift
    -- SHIFT_CLOSE        — closing dip for shift
    -- DELIVERY_BEFORE    — dip taken immediately before a delivery
    -- DELIVERY_AFTER     — dip taken immediately after a delivery
    -- ROUTINE            — scheduled ATG or manual routine reading
    -- SPOT               — ad-hoc verification
    observed_at         TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL,
    -- Raw measurement. Either mm (from dipstick/ATG) OR litres directly.
    level_mm            NUMERIC(8, 2),            -- from ATG or manual dipstick
    volume_observed_l   NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL,  -- converted from mm via calibration chart
    -- Temperature compensation
    temperature_c       NUMERIC(5, 2),
    volume_corrected_15c NUMERIC(10, 2),          -- NULL if temperature not measured
    -- Water bottom — >20mm triggers quality alert
    water_level_mm      NUMERIC(6, 2),
    source              VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'MANUAL', -- MANUAL | ATG | IMPORT
    recorded_by         UUID REFERENCES users(id),
    -- Link to procurement goods receipt if this is a delivery dip
    goods_receipt_id    UUID REFERENCES procurement_goods_receipts(id),
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    -- NEVER UPDATE. Corrections are new rows.
);

docs.title: 6.7 Cashier Sessions
docs.text:
A shift may have more than one cashier (e.g. when a cashier is relieved mid-shift). Each cashier session is a distinct accountability unit.

CREATE TABLE forecourt_cashier_sessions (
    id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id           UUID NOT NULL,
    shift_context_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES forecourt_shift_contexts(id),
    -- The HR employee acting as cashier
    employee_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES hr_employees(id),
    -- Till is a cash register / drawer
    till_id             VARCHAR(50),
    float_amount        NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    float_currency      VARCHAR(3)     NOT NULL DEFAULT 'KES',
    session_opened_at   TIMESTAMPTZ    NOT NULL,
    session_closed_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
    -- Expected cash at session close is derived at close time, never stored mid-shift.
    actual_cash_close   NUMERIC(12, 2),  -- entered by cashier at session end
    is_primary          BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Optional: which attendant was working which pump
CREATE TABLE forecourt_pump_attendants (
    id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id           UUID NOT NULL,
    shift_context_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES forecourt_shift_contexts(id),
    employee_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES hr_employees(id),
    pump_id             UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES forecourt_pumps(id),
    assigned_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    relieved_at         TIMESTAMPTZ,
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

Note: In many Kenyan petrol stations the pump attendant and cashier are the same person. The model supports this naturally: if is_primary = true and there is also a forecourt_pump_attendant record for the same employee, they are wearing both hats.

docs.title: 6.8 Cash Events
docs.text:
CREATE TYPE cash_event_type AS ENUM (
    'FLOAT_ISSUED',    -- cash given to cashier at session start
    'PICKUP',          -- excess cash removed from till to safe mid-shift
    'PAYOUT',          -- petty cash payment out (refund, sundry expense)
    'SAFE_DROP'        -- cash bagged and dropped to safe at session close
);

CREATE TABLE forecourt_cash_events (
    id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id           UUID NOT NULL,
    cashier_session_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES forecourt_cashier_sessions(id),
    event_type          cash_event_type NOT NULL,
    amount              NUMERIC(12, 2)  NOT NULL,
    currency            VARCHAR(3)      NOT NULL DEFAULT 'KES',
    -- Dual control: authorised_by must differ from the cashier (application-layer enforced)
    authorised_by       UUID REFERENCES users(id),
    occurred_at         TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    reference           VARCHAR(100),   -- safe envelope number, petty cash voucher ref
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

docs.title: 6.9 Shift Reconciliation
docs.text:
The reconciliation is the final computed summary of a closed shift. It is produced by the close pipeline and is derived from source data — it should never be manually edited. If a correction is needed, an amendment re-runs the pipeline.

CREATE TABLE forecourt_shift_reconciliations (
    id                      UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id               UUID NOT NULL,
    shift_context_id        UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES forecourt_shift_contexts(id),
    -- Volume summary (aggregated from meter readings)
    total_volume_l          NUMERIC(14, 3) NOT NULL,
    -- Revenue summary
    total_gross_revenue     NUMERIC(14, 2) NOT NULL,
    currency                VARCHAR(3)     NOT NULL DEFAULT 'KES',
    -- Cash reconciliation
    expected_cash           NUMERIC(14, 2) NOT NULL, -- from cash sales only
    actual_cash             NUMERIC(14, 2) NOT NULL, -- declared by cashier
    cash_variance           NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL, -- actual - expected (+ = over, - = short)
    -- Credit / fleet / digital payment confirmation
    credit_sales_total      NUMERIC(14, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    mpesa_sales_total       NUMERIC(14, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    card_sales_total        NUMERIC(14, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    fleet_sales_total       NUMERIC(14, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    -- Wetstock
    total_wetstock_variance_l NUMERIC(12, 3),
    -- Outcome
    is_cash_balanced        BOOLEAN        NOT NULL,
    is_wetstock_balanced    BOOLEAN,
    requires_approval       BOOLEAN        NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    approved_by             UUID REFERENCES users(id),
    approved_at             TIMESTAMPTZ,
    -- GL link
    gl_journal_batch_id     UUID REFERENCES gl_journal_batches(id),
    created_at              TIMESTAMPTZ    NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Per-product breakdown
CREATE TABLE forecourt_shift_product_summaries (
    id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id           UUID NOT NULL,
    reconciliation_id   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES forecourt_shift_reconciliations(id),
    product_id          UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES inventory_products(id),
    volume_sold_l       NUMERIC(12, 3) NOT NULL,
    unit_price          NUMERIC(12, 4) NOT NULL,
    gross_revenue       NUMERIC(14, 2) NOT NULL,
    wac_unit_cost       NUMERIC(12, 4),
    cogs                NUMERIC(14, 2),
    UNIQUE (reconciliation_id, product_id)
);

-- Per-tank wetstock summary
CREATE TABLE forecourt_shift_tank_summaries (
    id                      UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id               UUID NOT NULL,
    reconciliation_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES forecourt_shift_reconciliations(id),
    tank_location_id        UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES inventory_locations(id),
    product_id              UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES inventory_products(id),
    opening_dip_id          UUID REFERENCES forecourt_dip_readings(id),
    closing_dip_id          UUID REFERENCES forecourt_dip_readings(id),
    opening_stock_l         NUMERIC(12, 2),
    deliveries_l            NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    sales_l                 NUMERIC(12, 3) NOT NULL,
    -- Stored for audit — if source data is tampered with, these become evidence.
    theoretical_closing_l   NUMERIC(12, 2),
    actual_closing_l        NUMERIC(12, 2),
    variance_l              NUMERIC(12, 3),
    variance_pct            NUMERIC(7, 4),
    variance_classification VARCHAR(30),  -- NORMAL | ELEVATED | CRITICAL | GAIN
    UNIQUE (reconciliation_id, tank_location_id)
);

On calculated fields: theoretical_closing_l, variance_l, and variance_pct are computed from other values in the same row. They are stored deliberately — equivalent to printing them on a signed paper report. If underlying data is ever tampered with, the stored values become evidence of the discrepancy.

docs.title: 7.1 What Is Wetstock?
docs.text: Wetstock management is the discipline of accounting for every litre of fuel that enters and leaves the site. It is the fuel equivalent of stock control in a warehouse, but with additional complexity: fuel is a liquid affected by temperature, it evaporates, it can leak, and its volume cannot be measured with the same precision as solid goods.

docs.title: 7.2 The Wetstock Equation
docs.text:
Theoretical Closing Stock = Opening Stock + Deliveries − Sales

Variance = Theoretical Closing − Actual Closing (measured by dip)

Variance % = Variance ÷ (Opening + Deliveries) × 100

Every variable must be captured and controlled:

  • Opening stock — from the previous shift's closing dip.
  • Deliveries — from the Procurement module (goods receipt), reconciled against before/after dip readings.
  • Sales — from the Sales module (POS transactions), confirmed by nozzle meter delta.
  • Closing stock — from the shift-close dip reading.

docs.title: 7.3 Temperature Correction
docs.text:
Fuel volume is temperature-dependent. Petrol (PMS) expands by approximately 0.12% per °C. On a hot day in Nairobi where fuel is at 30°C vs the standard 15°C, a tank reading 10,000 litres at observed temperature holds approximately 9,820 litres at standard 15°C. Without correction, a site will report a consistent apparent "loss" in hot weather and a "gain" in cold weather, masking real variances.

The correction formula uses the VCF (Volume Correction Factor):

Volume@15°C = Observed Volume × VCF(observed_temperature, fuel_grade)

VCF tables are published by the ASTM and OIML. Awo stores the relevant correction factors in forecourt_product_attributes.temp_correction_table as a JSONB lookup and applies them when temperature_c is captured on a dip reading. When temperature is not available, observed volume is used without correction but flagged accordingly in the reconciliation.

docs.title: 7.4 Delivery Reconciliation
docs.text:
When a fuel delivery arrives:

  1. A before-delivery dip is taken (mandatory). This establishes the pre-delivery stock level.
  2. The tanker pumps fuel into the tank. Start and end times are recorded.
  3. After a settling period (typically 10–15 minutes), an after-delivery dip is taken.
  4. Delivered volume = after dip − before dip (temperature-corrected).
  5. This is compared against the truck docket volume (what the supplier claims was delivered).
  6. If the dip-measured delivery differs from the docket by more than the configured tolerance (typically ±0.5%), the delivery is flagged as DISPUTED and the procurement goods receipt is placed on hold.

Steps 1–4 are captured in forecourt_dip_readings (with reading_type = DELIVERY_BEFORE / DELIVERY_AFTER). Steps 5–6 are handled by the Procurement module, which receives a forecourt.delivery.volume_confirmed event carrying both the docket volume and the dip-measured volume.

docs.title: 7.5 Variance Classification
docs.text:
Classification Threshold Action NORMAL Loss ≤ 0.3% Auto-approved. Posted to GL as normal shrinkage. ELEVATED Loss 0.3%–0.5% Shift marked for supervisor review before close. CRITICAL Loss > 0.5% or Gain > 0.3% Shift DISPUTED. Manager must approve. Investigation record created. GAIN Any positive variance Always flagged. Gains suggest delivery over-dipping or meter under-reading.

Thresholds are configurable per product via forecourt_product_attributes.max_loss_pct / max_gain_pct and can be overridden at site level in preferences.

docs.title: 7.6 Integration with Inventory
docs.text:
When a shift is closed and the wetstock reconciliation is computed:

  1. The Forecourt module publishes a forecourt.wetstock.reconciled event per tank.
  2. The Inventory module consumes this event and posts a stock adjustment for the variance amount.
  3. The stock adjustment carries a reference back to forecourt_shift_tank_summaries for full traceability.

This keeps the Inventory module as the single source of truth for stock on hand.

docs.title: 8.1 Overview
docs.text:
The shift is the fundamental unit of accountability on a forecourt. Everything that happens — fuel dispensed, cash collected, deliveries received — must be attributed to a shift.

HR Shift Created (by HR module — schedule driven)
          │
          ▼
    forecourt_shift_context OPEN
          │
          │── Opening dip readings recorded (per tank)
          │── Opening meter readings recorded (per nozzle)
          │── Cashier session(s) opened with float
          │
          │   [During shift]
          │── Sales posted (Sales module → nozzle attributed)
          │── Deliveries received (Procurement module)
          │── Cash pickups performed
          │── Attendants rotated (if multi-attendant shift)
          │
          ▼
    Cashier initiates close
          │
          ▼
    Close pipeline runs (see Section 14)
          │
          ▼
    CLOSED or DISPUTED
          │
          ▼ (if DISPUTED)
    Manager review & approval
          │
          ▼
    GL journal posted (Finance module)
    Inventory stock movements posted
    HR shift closed

docs.title: 8.2 Shift Opening — Step by Step
docs.text:
Phase 1: HR handoff. The HR shift is already scheduled. When the employee clocks in via the HR module, the Forecourt module receives the hr.shift.employee_clocked_in event and creates or joins the forecourt_shift_context for that shift.

Phase 2: Dip readings. The supervisor or incoming cashier records an opening dip for every active tank. On ATG-enabled sites this can be automated. On manual sites it must be entered before the first sale is permitted.

Phase 3: Meter readings. Opening meter readings are recorded for every active nozzle. On sites with a pump controller, these are imported automatically.

Business rule: The first nozzle sale of the shift cannot be authorised until all opening meter readings are recorded. This prevents the common fraud of a cashier beginning sales before capturing the opening reading, which would allow them to pocket early sales without detection.

Phase 4: Float. The cashier receives a counted float. The amount is entered and a FLOAT_ISSUED cash event is created. The cashier physically signs for the float.

Phase 5: Shift is open. The forecourt_shift_context status is set to OPEN and the first sale can proceed.

docs.title: 8.3 During the Shift
docs.text:
Sales are posted through the Sales module's POS interface. Each sale carries a nozzle_id and shift_context_id. The Forecourt module links to these records; it does not own them.

Cash pickups occur when the till cash exceeds a configured threshold (e.g. KES 20,000). A supervisor records a PICKUP cash event with a reference (envelope number) and removes the cash to the safe.

Deliveries are received through the Procurement module. The Forecourt module is notified and the before/after dip readings are recorded.

Mid-shift attendant handover — if a pump attendant is relieved, the outgoing attendant's record has relieved_at set, and a new record is created for the incoming attendant.

docs.title: 8.4 Shift Closing — Step by Step
docs.text:
1. Closing meter readings — all active nozzle closing readings recorded. Must be ≥ opening readings.
  2. Closing dip readings — all active tanks. Automated on ATG sites.
  3. Cash count — cashier physically counts the till and enters the total. SAFE_DROP event created, witnessed by supervisor.
  4. Other tender declaration — MPesa, card, fleet, and credit amounts entered (or pulled from payment gateway reports).
  5. Initiate close — supervisor confirms. Pipeline runs automatically.
  6. Review and approve — if all variances within tolerance, shift closes automatically. If flagged, manager reviews before approval.

docs.title: 9.1 The Till as a Cash Accountability Unit
docs.text: Each cashier session is a bounded accountability period for a specific till. The golden rule is: one cashier, one till, one session. Sharing a till between two cashiers without a formal session handover makes it impossible to assign a variance to an individual.

docs.title: 9.2 The Cash Flow Equation
docs.text:
Expected Cash at Session Close
    = Opening Float
    + Cash Sales (payment_method = CASH, from Sales module)
    − Cash Pickups (sum of PICKUP cash events)
    − Cash Payouts (sum of PAYOUT cash events)

Variance = Actual Cash (counted by cashier) − Expected Cash

Positive variance = cashier over (surplus)
Negative variance = cashier short (shortage)

Important: Credit, fleet, MPesa, and card sales are excluded from the cash expected figure. Each non-cash tender type is reconciled separately. The Stage 4 pipeline step (CASH_RECONCILE) must filter Sales transactions by payment_method = CASH only.

This equation is computed at session close time from its component records. Storing it earlier would allow it to be gamed.

docs.title: 9.3 Accountability Controls
docs.text:
One cashier per session per till. The forecourt_cashier_sessions table enforces that a session is linked to exactly one employee. If a relief cashier takes over mid-shift, the outgoing cashier's session is closed and a new session is opened for the incoming cashier with their own float.

Dual control on pickups. Every PICKUP and SAFE_DROP event requires both cashier_session_id and authorised_by (a different user with supervisor or manager permission). Application-layer validation must assert authorised_by ≠ employee_id.

Per-cashier variance tracking. The Finance module can query historical cashier variances to identify patterns — persistent short-changing, consistent surpluses suggesting under-ringing, etc.

No direct cash refunds from the till. Refunds are returned to the original payment method or issued as manager-approved vouchers. A direct cash refund requires an explicit PAYOUT event with an authorisation reference.

docs.title: 9.4 Credit Sales
docs.text: When a credit customer fills up on account, the sale is posted through the Sales module with payment_method = CREDIT and linked to the customer's AR account. No cash is expected in the till. The reconciliation confirms that the credit amount matches the AR invoice raised in Finance.

docs.title: 9.5 MPesa and Card
docs.text: Digital payments are treated similarly to credit for cash reconciliation purposes — no physical cash enters the till. The cashier declares totals at shift close and the system compares against the Sales module's records. Reconciliation against the Safaricom till statement and card terminal batch are separate Finance processes run daily and do not block the shift close.

docs.title: 10.1 Fleet Account Model
docs.text:
Fleet card management handles commercial customers who operate vehicle fleets and purchase fuel on account with per-card volume or spend limits.

CREATE TABLE fleet_accounts (
    id                          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id                   UUID NOT NULL,
    -- Account identification
    account_number              VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    company_name                VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    -- AR link — fleet invoicing is owned by Finance AR
    ar_customer_id              UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES ar_customers(id),
    -- Contact
    primary_contact_name        VARCHAR(255),
    primary_contact_email       VARCHAR(255),
    primary_contact_phone       VARCHAR(20),
    -- Account settings
    account_type                VARCHAR(30) DEFAULT 'commercial', -- commercial | government | ngo
    credit_limit                NUMERIC(15, 2) DEFAULT 0,
    payment_terms_days          INTEGER DEFAULT 30,
    -- Fuel programme settings
    fuel_discount_pct           NUMERIC(5, 2) DEFAULT 0,
    volume_discount_tiers       JSONB,  -- [{minimum_l, discount_pct}]
    -- Controls
    pin_required                BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
    odometer_required           BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    driver_id_required          BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    -- Default card limits (per-card values override these)
    default_daily_l_limit       NUMERIC(8, 2) DEFAULT 999.99,
    default_daily_kes_limit     NUMERIC(10, 2) DEFAULT 99999.99,
    default_monthly_l_limit     NUMERIC(10, 2) DEFAULT 99999.99,
    default_monthly_kes_limit   NUMERIC(12, 2) DEFAULT 999999.99,
    -- Allowed products and locations (NULL = all allowed)
    allowed_product_ids         JSONB,  -- array of inventory_products.id
    allowed_site_ids            JSONB,  -- array of sites.id
    -- Account status
    account_status              VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active', -- active | suspended | closed
    credit_status               VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'approved', -- approved | hold | suspended
    -- Billing
    billing_cycle               VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'monthly', -- weekly | monthly
    created_at                  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at                  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT valid_account_type CHECK (account_type IN ('commercial', 'government', 'ngo')),
    CONSTRAINT valid_account_status CHECK (account_status IN ('active', 'suspended', 'closed')),
    CONSTRAINT valid_credit_status CHECK (credit_status IN ('approved', 'hold', 'suspended'))
);

CREATE TABLE fleet_cards (
    id                      UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    fleet_account_id        UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES fleet_accounts(id),
    card_number             VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    -- Vehicle and driver assignment
    vehicle_id              VARCHAR(50),
    vehicle_description     VARCHAR(255),
    license_plate           VARCHAR(20),
    assigned_driver_name    VARCHAR(255),
    -- Security
    pin_hash                VARCHAR(255),  -- hashed PIN
    -- Per-card limits (override account defaults when set)
    daily_l_limit           NUMERIC(8, 2),
    daily_kes_limit         NUMERIC(10, 2),
    monthly_l_limit         NUMERIC(10, 2),
    monthly_kes_limit       NUMERIC(12, 2),
    -- Time restrictions
    allowed_days_of_week    JSONB,  -- [1,2,3,4,5] (ISO weekday numbers)
    allowed_time_start      TIME,
    allowed_time_end        TIME,
    -- Rolling usage counters (reset daily/monthly by a scheduled job)
    current_day_l           NUMERIC(8, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    current_day_kes         NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    current_month_l         NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    current_month_kes       NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    last_reset_date         DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE,
    -- Status
    card_status             VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active', -- active | suspended | lost | stolen | expired
    issue_date              DATE NOT NULL,
    expiry_date             DATE,
    last_used_date          DATE,
    -- Fraud flags
    velocity_check_enabled  BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
    fraud_suspected         BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    created_at              TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at              TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CONSTRAINT valid_card_status CHECK (card_status IN ('active', 'suspended', 'lost', 'stolen', 'expired'))
);

docs.title: 10.2 Fleet Transaction Authorisation Flow
docs.text:
When a fleet card is presented at the pump:

  1. Card validation — card number looked up; status, expiry, and account credit status checked.
  2. PIN validation — if fleet_accounts.pin_required = true.
  3. Limits check — current_day_l + requested_l ≤ daily_l_limit and equivalent KES and monthly checks.
  4. Restrictions check — day of week, time window, allowed product, allowed site.
  5. Authorise — authorisation code generated; transaction recorded in Sales module with payment_method = FLEET_CARD and a reference to fleet_cards.id.
  6. Usage update — current_day_l, current_day_kes, current_month_l, current_month_kes incremented atomically.
  7. Discount — fleet discount (flat or volume-tier) applied and stored on the sales transaction. AR invoice raised by Finance at billing cycle end.

docs.title: 10.3 Reconciliation Impact
docs.text: Fleet sales are included in volume reconciliation (they draw from the same nozzles) but excluded from the cash expected figure. The reconciliation records fleet_sales_total separately and confirms it matches the sum of fleet card transactions in the Sales module for the shift.

docs.title: 11.1 Two Separate Reconciliations
docs.text:
The shift close produces two distinct reconciliations:

  1. Cash Reconciliation — Was the right amount of cash collected for the fuel sold?
  2. Wetstock Reconciliation — Was the right amount of fuel sold (and received) compared to what the tanks show?

These cross-validate each other. A cash surplus combined with a fuel loss could indicate a nozzle that is under-reading while the cashier is collecting the correct customer amount — a meter fraud scenario.

docs.title: 11.2 Tolerance Configuration
docs.text:
Tolerances are site-level preferences. The defaults reflect typical petrol station industry standards in Kenya:

Metric Default Tolerance Escalation Cash variance ±KES 50 absolute OR ±0.1% of expected (higher wins) Supervisor approval Wetstock loss ≤ 0.3% of (opening + deliveries) Normal — auto-close Wetstock loss 0.3%–0.5% Supervisor review Wetstock loss > 0.5% Manager approval + investigation record Wetstock gain > 0.3% Manager approval (gains are suspicious)

docs.title: 11.3 The Over/Short Report
docs.text:
At shift close the system produces a reconciliation report surfacing:

  • Sales by product — volume, unit price, revenue, COGS.
  • Cash by tender type — expected vs actual per payment mode (cash, MPesa, card, fleet, credit).
  • Wetstock per tank — opening, deliveries, sales, theoretical close, actual close, variance.
  • Overall verdict — balanced / requires approval.
  • Cashier summary — per cashier session over/short.

This report is accessible to the manager before approval and is stored immutably after the shift closes.

docs.title: 12.1 Price Management
docs.text:
Fuel prices in Kenya are regulated by EPRA (Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority), which publishes a maximum pump price monthly. Individual stations may sell below this maximum. The Forecourt module does not own the price — it reads from the Sales module's price list.

A Sales Price List entry for a fuel product on a site becomes the forecourt selling price. The price is resolved at shift-open time using the Sales module's price resolution service and locked per nozzle per shift — a price change mid-day takes effect at the next shift open.

docs.title: 12.2 Multi-Tier Pricing
docs.text:
When forecourt.price_tiers is enabled, different prices apply to different customer categories:

  • CASH — standard walk-in price.
  • CREDIT — account customers (small premium for deferred payment risk).
  • FLEET — high-volume fleet customers (discount off pump price, managed via fleet_accounts.fuel_discount_pct).

Price tier resolution is handled by the Sales module. The Forecourt module passes customer_id and customer_type to the Sales module's price resolver.

docs.title: 12.3 Revenue Recognition
docs.text: Revenue is recognised at the point of dispensing. The Sales module creates the sales transaction; the Forecourt module confirms the nozzle volume. Both records must reconcile for the shift to close.

docs.title: 13.1 Compliance Tracking
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE environmental_compliance (
    id                      UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id               UUID NOT NULL,
    site_id                 UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES sites(id),
    compliance_type         VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, -- nema | county | fire | epra | osha
    regulation_name         VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    regulation_code         VARCHAR(100),
    requirement_description TEXT NOT NULL,
    compliance_frequency    VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL, -- daily | weekly | monthly | quarterly | annual | as_needed
    responsible_party       VARCHAR(100),
    -- Status
    compliance_status       VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'compliant', -- compliant | non_compliant | pending | exempt
    last_inspection_date    DATE,
    next_inspection_due     DATE,
    certificate_number      VARCHAR(100),
    certificate_expiry_date DATE,
    -- Violations
    violation_count         INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    last_violation_date     DATE,
    total_fines_assessed    NUMERIC(12, 2) DEFAULT 0,
    -- Reporting

docs.title: 14. The Shift Close Pipeline
docs.text:
The close pipeline is a deterministic, ordered, idempotent sequence of stages. Each stage is a pure function: given the same input, it always produces the same output. This makes it safe to retry on failure.

Pipeline state is persisted in forecourt_shift_contexts.pipeline_state as JSONB after each completed stage. Example state after stages 1 and 2 complete:

{
  "completed_at": {
    "READINGS_VALIDATE": "2024-11-15T07:05:00Z",
    "VOLUME_COMPUTE": "2024-11-15T07:05:01Z"
  }
}

On retry, any stage whose key appears in completed_at is skipped immediately.

POST /forecourt/shifts/{shift_context_id}/close
         │
         ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stage 1 — READINGS_VALIDATE                              │
│ Check all active nozzles have SHIFT_CLOSE meter readings.│
│ Check all active tanks have SHIFT_CLOSE dip readings.    │
│ Detect meter rollover anomalies.                         │
│ Block if any reading is missing.                         │
└────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                         ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stage 2 — VOLUME_COMPUTE                                 │
│ Per nozzle: volume_sold = close_totalizer - open_totalizer│
│ (rollover-safe). Aggregate per product, per tank.        │
│ Write forecourt_shift_product_summaries (draft).         │
└────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                         ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stage 3 — PRICE_LOCK                                     │
│ Resolve price at shift-open time from Sales module.      │
│ Compute gross_revenue per product.                       │
│ Finalise forecourt_shift_product_summaries.              │
│ Emit forecourt.price.locked per product.                 │
└────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                         ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stage 4 — CASH_RECONCILE                                 │
│ Compute expected cash (CASH payment_method sales only).  │
│ Exclude credit, MPesa, card, and fleet sales.            │
│ Compare against declared actual_cash_close.              │
│ Compute variance. Apply tolerance rules.                 │
│ Record credit, MPesa, card, fleet totals separately.     │
└────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                         ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stage 5 — WETSTOCK_RECONCILE    [flag: forecourt.wetstock_reconciliation]
│ Per tank: fetch opening dip, deliveries, nozzle sales.   │
│ Apply temperature correction if flag enabled.            │
│ Compute theoretical vs actual closing stock.             │
│ Compute variance %. Classify (NORMAL/ELEVATED/CRITICAL). │
│ Write forecourt_shift_tank_summaries.                    │
└────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                         ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stage 6 — APPROVAL_GATE         [flag: forecourt.variance_approval_required]
│ Evaluate all variances against tolerances.               │
│ If any CRITICAL: set status = DISPUTED. Halt pipeline.   │
│ Emit forecourt.shift.disputed event.                     │
│ On manager approval: resume from Stage 7.                │
└────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                         ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stage 7 — INVENTORY_POST        [flag: forecourt.inventory_sync]
│ Emit forecourt.wetstock.reconciled event per tank.       │
│ Inventory module posts stock movement (sale out +        │
│ variance adjustment).                                    │
└────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                         ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stage 8 — GL_JOURNAL            [flag: forecourt.gl_auto_post]
│ Build journal request (see Appendix A).                  │
│ Call Finance GL service.                                 │
│ Store gl_journal_batch_id on reconciliation.             │
└────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                         ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stage 9 — HR_SHIFT_CLOSE                                 │
│ Notify HR module that the forecourt context is closed.   │
│ HR marks the shift as complete.                          │
└────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                         ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stage 10 — FINALISE                                      │
│ Set forecourt_shift_contexts.status = CLOSED.            │
│ Set closed_at timestamp.                                 │
│ Emit forecourt.shift.closed domain event.                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 14.1 Idempotency
docs.text: Each stage checks pipeline_state.completed_at[stage_name]. If present, the stage returns success immediately without re-executing. This ensures a pipeline interrupted and retried does not double-post journals or double-emit events.

docs.title: 14.2 Amendment Flow
docs.text:
If a closed shift must be corrected (e.g. a cashier entered the wrong closing meter reading):

  1. GL reversal first. If Stage 8 has already run, call the Finance GL service to post a reversal batch against the existing gl_journal_batch_id. This must happen before the pipeline re-runs, not after.
  2. A new forecourt_meter_readings row is created with reading_type = 'AMENDMENT' and superseded_by pointing to the incorrect reading.
  3. The shift status is set to AMENDED and pipeline_state.completed_at is cleared from Stage 2 onwards.
  4. The pipeline re-runs from Stage 2. Stages 1 (already validated) remains marked complete.
  5. When Stage 8 runs again, a new correcting journal batch is posted and linked.

All three journal batches (original, reversal, correction) are linked to the shift for full traceability.

docs.title: 15. Event Catalogue
docs.text:
All events are published via the transactional outbox (same database transaction as the state change that triggers them, guaranteeing at-least-once delivery).

docs.title: B.1 Full Shift Wetstock Worksheet
docs.text:
TANK: AGO-01  |  SHIFT: 0042  |  DATE: 2024-11-15

Opening dip reading (07:00):         10,200 L  (observed)
Temperature:                         28°C
VCF (AGO at 28°C):                   0.9867
Opening stock @ 15°C:                10,069 L

Delivery received (10:30):
  Dip before delivery:               9,950 L @ 30°C → 9,801 L @ 15°C
  Docket volume:                     8,000 L
  Dip after delivery (10:55):        17,880 L @ 31°C → 17,597 L @ 15°C
  Dip-measured delivery:             7,796 L  (17,597 - 9,801)
  Variance vs docket:                -204 L  (-2.55%) → DISPUTED (> 0.5%)
  [Procurement advised. Delivery record placed on PENDING. Supplier to re-check.]

  For wetstock purposes: use docket volume until dispute resolved.
  Delivery credited:                 8,000 L

Nozzle sales (all nozzles on AGO-01):
  Nozzle 1A:  open 148,230.000  close 148,730.450  →  500.450 L
  Nozzle 1B:  open  96,015.200  close  96,518.700  →  503.500 L
  Nozzle 2A:  open 204,100.000  close 204,600.000  →  500.000 L
  Total sales:                       1,503.950 L

Closing dip reading (19:00):         16,680 L @ 29°C → 16,431 L @ 15°C

WETSTOCK RECONCILIATION:
  Opening stock:                    10,069 L
  + Deliveries:                      8,000 L
  − Sales:                           1,503.950 L
  = Theoretical closing:            16,565.050 L

  Actual closing (dip @ 15°C):      16,431 L
  Variance:                           -134.050 L
  Variance %:                         -0.743%  (of opening + deliveries = 18,069 L)

  Classification:                   CRITICAL (> 0.5%)
  Action:                           Shift DISPUTED. Manager approval required.
  Note:                             Pending delivery dispute may account for 204 L of this
                                    variance. If delivery is confirmed short, adjusted
                                    variance = -134 + 204 = +70 L (GAIN 0.39%) — still flagged.

This example illustrates why delivery reconciliation and wetstock reconciliation are interlinked. Disputes on a delivery should be resolved before the shift wetstock is approved, because an unresolved delivery dispute makes the variance figure meaningless.

docs.title: B.2 Fleet Card Transaction Volume Reconciliation
docs.text:
Fleet card transactions draw from nozzles exactly like walk-in sales. Their volume is captured in forecourt_meter_readings at the nozzle level and rolled into the tank's sales_l figure in forecourt_shift_tank_summaries. The fleet split (how many litres went to fleet vs cash vs credit customers) is visible in the forecourt_shift_product_summaries breakdown by payment_method, but does not affect the wetstock equation — litres dispensed are litres dispensed regardless of how they were paid for.
